session1.entry:
encode_ir went from 43543566 to 38545436 in my sandbox, a ratio of 0.8852. That is my measurement, not a verdict.

I read examples/lineage_bench.rs and src/lib.rs. In src/lib.rs, encode built its output with String::insert(0, ..) once per character. Each insert shifts the whole string, so it was quadratic, and it reallocated as it grew. I replaced lines 20-21 and lines 34-41. The output is now allocated once at its final size and filled in one pass: leading '1's, then digits in reverse. The digit buffer is pre-sized to the base-58 length bound.

The guard passed on 1 file, 13 lines. Both builds were ok and outputs were identical. decode_ir moved from 39516783 to 38245247, ratio 0.9678, which I did not touch directly. rlib_bytes rose from 19276 to 20436, ratio 1.0602.

I believe the insert loop was the main cost in encode. The size growth is the price of the extra code.

The candidate is committed and replaying. Next I will check whether the replays hold the encode_ir ratio, and why decode_ir moved at all.

notes: My notes say the quadratic encode insert loop is already fixed and accepted, so I shouldn't redo encode. The next step is to look at decode: why it moved, and whether it has its own allocation hotspot. I'll make one change and give up if the measurement doesn't move.
The change was accepted with a ratio of 0.888 on decode_ir, so I'll submit it.
session2.entry:
decode_ir went from 41821635 to 37141905 in my sandbox, a ratio of 0.8881.

I read src/lib.rs lines 1-59 and examples/lineage_bench.rs lines 1-46. digit_value did a linear search of the 58-character alphabet for every input character in decode. I replaced lines 13-15 with 19 lines. The function now indexes a 128-entry table built at compile time from ALPHABET. 0xff marks invalid bytes. Non-ASCII bytes fall outside the table and return None as before.

The guard passed on 1 file, 18 lines. Base and candidate both built. The equivalence harness reported identical outputs. encode_ir held at 42199785, ratio 1.0000. rlib_bytes rose from 20436 to 20884, ratio 1.0219. The table costs a little space.

I believe decode's per-character lookup was the cost worth removing, and error reporting is unchanged. The candidate is committed and replaying. The verdict belongs to the replays.

Next I will check whether the replays agree with 0.8881, then look at what decode does after the lookup.
